chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no Prophet nor a successor of a Prophet who remains in the earth for more than three days, until his soul, and his bones, and his flesh are raised to the sky; and rather, they are sent to the places of their traces, and they deliver greetings to them from afar, and they hear them in the places of their traces from nearby.
ai.seo_question: How long do Prophets and Imams remain on earth after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia doctrine of the Imams' continued spiritual presence (Hudhur) after death, distinguishing their unique status from ordinary prophets by emphasizing their accessibility through their graves or shrines. It underscores the concept of 'Barzakh' where the soul remains connected to the physical world, allowing for reciprocal salutations between the living and the deceased Imams. This supports the theological basis for visiting graves (Ziyarat) as a means of drawing near to God through the intercession and spiritual proximity of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Ziyad Bin Abu Al Hallal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a Prophet<sup>as</sup> nor a successor<sup>as</sup> of a Prophet<sup>as</sup> who remains in the earth (after his<sup>as</sup> passing away), for more than three days, until his<sup>as</sup> soul, and his<sup>as</sup> bones, and his<sup>as</sup> flesh are Raised to the sky; and rather, they (people) are going to the places of their<sup>as</sup> traces, and they are delivering the greetings from afar, and they<sup>as</sup> are hearing them in the places of their<sup>as</sup> traces, from nearby’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ziyad ibn abu al-Hallal who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

no one of the prophets and the executors of the will of the prophets remain on earth for more than three days, within which time his Ruh (spirit), bones and flesh are taken to the heaven. People come only to the places where their marks are left. They convey and express their al-Salam from distant places and they hear them nearby in the places where their marks are left.”
